prepared_by: prep-reconcile (multi-candidate-merge over prep-fast-pass + candidate-1/2/3 + grep backstop)
synthesis: Admin 'Login to Scout' force-login intermittently fails with no usable error. Observed 2026-09-16 during a Premier Adjusters demo: it worked earlier in the admin session, then 'stopped loading' for 3 different Scout users consecutively. PR #410 (83fb68d24, merged 2026-09-15 18:01 UTC) is CONFIRMED DEPLOYED before the incident (deploy ac85618e0 at 2026-09-15 18:18 UTC), so the demo ran post-#410 code and the original duplicate-GET bug is ruled out. Reconcile refuted two of the three competing root-cause hypotheses from ground truth and demoted the third: (a) C2 new-tab cookie propagation is REFUTED (same_site=lax + path=/ + same-origin top-level GET always sends the session cookie; tabs share one cookie jar); (b) C1 'admin_impersonator cleared mid-flow' is REFUTED as stated (invalidate at ImpersonateController:35 and the re-put at :57 are in the same request, atomic before redirect); (c) C-fast/C3 Session::push cross-driver accumulation is a CONFIRMED DEFECT but INSUFFICIENT alone — revokeTracked() has exactly 3 call sites, all in ImpersonateController (:32/:83/:94), none in the force-login path, so consecutive force-logins inside one impersonation never trigger it. Two defects no candidate found are now confirmed from code: (1) GET /auth/impersonate/exit-admin silently strips admin_impersonator AND mass-revokes every tracked force token, then redirect()->back(), leaving the stale Livewire table still rendering a now-403 'Login to Scout' button — the single best fit for 'worked, then stopped for 3 consecutive users, no error'; (2) the Scout PWA reads its bearer from the origin-shared localStorage 'scanner_token' on every request (fetch.js:24) while forceAuthenticate() overwrites it (auth.js:207), so each new force-login hijacks the REST identity of every already-open Scout tab. Root cause remains COMPETING-OPEN: the discriminating facts (what 'stopped loading' actually was on the wire, whether the admin re-impersonated or exited admin mode, whether tabs stayed open) are unanswered, and exitAdminMode() writes no activity_log row so the incident cannot be reconstructed retroactively.

root_cause_hypotheses.label: Exit Admin Mode silently strips the gate and mass-revokes force tokens
root_cause_hypotheses.origin: reconcile (found by none of the candidates)
root_cause_hypotheses.mechanism: GET /auth/impersonate/exit-admin (routes/web.php:45) is a plain <a href> in the persistent Filament impersonation banner (resources/views/filament/hooks/impersonate.blade.php:6). ImpersonateController::exitAdminMode() (:92-99) calls ScoutForceTokens::revokeTracked() -> deletes EVERY force token minted in this session (all drivers), then session()->forget('admin_impersonator'), then redirect()->back(). The admin lands on the same page with no confirmation and no flash message. The Filament table is not re-rendered, so the force_login_portal action's visible() check (ScoutUsersResource:353) is not re-evaluated and the button keeps rendering. Every subsequent click now hits abort_unless(session()->has('admin_impersonator'), 403) (ClarityScoutForceLoginController:16) and the new tab shows a bare 403 — indistinguishable from 'stopped loading' to a demo audience. Being a GET, it is also reachable by browser history replay, a prefetch, or a stray click.
explains: one-shot transition rather than a flaky race
root_cause_hypotheses.why_still_open: Cannot be confirmed from code alone — needs Q2/Q4/Q7. exitAdminMode() logs NO activity row (contrast leave() at :75-81 which does), so there is no audit trail to check. Force-login 403 rejections are also unlogged (the activity() call at ClarityScoutForceLoginController:26 sits AFTER both aborts).

root_cause_hypotheses.label: Cross-tab localStorage bearer-token collision
root_cause_hypotheses.origin: reconcile (found by none of the candidates)
root_cause_hypotheses.mechanism: authHeaders() re-reads localStorage.getItem('scanner_token') on EVERY request (resources/js/clarity-scout/lib/fetch.js:24) rather than using the Pinia store. forceAuthenticate() writes scanner_token/scanner_user/scanner_kit into localStorage (stores/auth.js:207-209), which is origin-scoped and shared by every tab. So force-logging Driver B overwrites the credential that Driver A's still-open tab uses: tab A renders Driver A's chrome but every REST call authenticates as B (then C). fetchUser() then writes the other driver's user/kit back into shared localStorage (auth.js:189-190), flipping tab A's identity. ClarityScoutMiddleware:25 accepts the force ability as a hard bypass, so these mismatched requests return 200 with the WRONG driver's data — no error anywhere. Echo is NOT affected (connectEcho bakes the token into the Echo config at construction, lib/echo.js:40), producing a split-brain tab: realtime on driver A, REST on driver C. forceAuthenticate() also calls clearApiCache() (auth.js:198), purging the shared SW API cache for all open tabs. A plain /scout reload in any tab picks up whichever driver was force-logged-in last (main.js:22).
explains: why it only bit once the admin worked through several drivers
root_cause_hypotheses.why_still_open: Confirmed as a defect independent of the incident. Whether it renders as 'stopped loading' (vs silently wrong data) depends on Q5, and on whether the affected drivers were in different orgs (Q3) — if so, a tab labelled one org's driver was displaying another org's driver data during a customer demo.
root_cause_hypotheses.tenancy_note: If the 3 drivers spanned orgs, this is a cross-org data-display defect, not merely a UX bug. Treat as security-adjacent until Q3 is answered.

root_cause_hypotheses.label: Session::push flat accumulation -> revokeTracked cross-driver mass revocation (C-fast / C3)
root_cause_hypotheses.origin: prep-fast-pass + candidate-3 (candidate-3 scored it 85 and named it THE root cause)
root_cause_hypotheses.mechanism: ScoutForceTokens::mintFor() pushes each minted token id onto a single flat session array (ScoutForceTokens.php:49) with no driver scoping. revokeTracked() Session::pull()s the whole array and bulk-deletes every id (:62,:68). After force-logging drivers A, B, C the array holds all three, so the next revokeTracked() kills all three tabs at once.
root_cause_hypotheses.demotion_reason: Verified with rg: revokeTracked() has exactly 3 call sites, all in ImpersonateController (:32 impersonate, :83 leave, :94 exitAdminMode). It is NOT called on the force-login path. prune() is correctly scoped to $driver->tokens() (:77-91) and KEEP_PER_DRIVER=3 is per-driver, so three different drivers keep three tokens each and never prune one another. Therefore consecutive force-logins WITHIN one continuous impersonation cannot trigger this. Candidate-3's 85 confidence over-claimed: it asserted revocation 'fires on impersonation exit/entry' and then attributed a symptom that occurred without either.
root_cause_hypotheses.still_in_scope_because: It is a real defect that fires whenever the admin re-impersonates (:32) or exits (:83/:94) — and via :94 it is the revocation half of H1. Fix regardless.
root_cause_hypotheses.becomes_primary_if: Q2 answers that the admin re-impersonated (e.g. to switch org) between the working force-login and the failures.

root_cause_hypotheses.label: admin_impersonator cleared by session invalidate mid-flow -> silent 403 (C1)
root_cause_hypotheses.refutation: ImpersonateController::impersonate() performs session()->invalidate() (:35) and session()->put('admin_impersonator', ...) (:57) inside the SAME request, before the redirect at :69. There is no window in which a later force-login observes a half-built session. Candidate-1's claim rested on reading the two line numbers as separate events; the request boundary refutes it.
root_cause_hypotheses.residual_variant_kept: A genuinely open 403 mechanism in the same area: config/session.php:35 sets lifetime=120 minutes idle. Force-login tabs authenticate to /api/scout/* with Sanctum bearer tokens, which never touch the admin's web session, so an admin who works only inside Scout tabs lets the admin-panel session idle-expire; the next force-login click then legitimately 403s. Plausible across a long demo. Needs Q5 (was it a 403 page?) plus the incident timeline.
root_cause_hypotheses.secondary_variant_kept: Concurrency, not invalidation: two near-simultaneous force-login GETs (prefetch / double-click) both Session::push. With no per-request session locking the later write can clobber the earlier, orphaning a minted token id so it is never revoked on exit — a gate-bypassing token that outlives the impersonation (up to the 60-min TTL). Security-adjacent; low probability; worth a test.

root_cause_hypotheses.label: New-tab session/cookie propagation is intermittent -> silent 403 (C2)
root_cause_hypotheses.refutation: config/session.php sets same_site='lax' (:202), path='/' (:146), partitioned=false (:215). Opening a same-origin URL via shouldOpenInNewTab (target=_blank) is a top-level GET navigation, which is exactly the case SameSite=Lax permits; and tabs in one browser profile share a single cookie jar — the Laravel session cookie is not per-tab. No mechanism exists for a new tab to fail to send it. Candidate-2's own evidence was inference only ('may not propagate', 'could be SameSite=Strict') with no file:line, and it did not read config/session.php; grounded-beats-confident applies.
root_cause_hypotheses.rejected_fix_warning: Candidate-2's recommended fix (approach_1: replace the session check with a signed URL) must NOT be adopted on this reasoning. It removes the staff-allowlist gate (ImpersonateController:43-58) from the only thing guarding a token that hard-bypasses the kit, permission, and feature-flag checks (ClarityScoutMiddleware:25, channels.php:30). A signed URL is bearer-equivalent: forwardable, loggable, and replayable within its window. Candidate-2's approach_4 (persist admin_impersonator on the users table) would also widen blast radius across ~60 unrelated admin_impersonator consumers — see missed_caller_candidates.conditional_blast_radius.

scope.summary: Diagnose and fix the silent-failure surface around Scout admin force-login. Three confirmed defects to fix independent of incident attribution: (1) exitAdminMode()/force-login rejections are silent and unaudited; (2) force-token session tracking is a flat cross-driver array; (3) the Scout PWA's bearer lives in origin-shared localStorage so concurrent force-login tabs hijack each other's identity. Add the missing regression test for consecutive force-logins of DIFFERENT drivers. Surface an explicit reason on every intentional block. Preserve all PR #410 behaviour (duplicate-GET tolerance, KEEP_PER_DRIVER=3 pruning, service-worker carve-out, client 401 reason surfacing).

proposed_changes.change: Scope the tracking structure per driver instead of a flat list: SESSION_KEY becomes a driver-keyed map (e.g. [driverId => [tokenIds]]). mintFor() pushes into that driver's bucket; revokeTracked() gains an optional ?User $driver to revoke one driver, defaulting to all. Keep KEEP_PER_DRIVER=3 and prune() untouched.
proposed_changes.reason: Line 49 appends to one flat array with no driver scoping and line 62/68 bulk-deletes every id, so one exit kills every open tab across all drivers (H3).
proposed_changes.caution: Do NOT implement the 'clear the array on each mint' alternative that candidate-3 offered as a simpler option — it re-breaks the exact duplicate-GET case PR #410 fixed (test_re_login_leaves_the_previously_issued_token_usable, ClarityScoutForceLoginControllerTest:87).

proposed_changes.change: Make exitAdminMode() observable: log an activity('impersonation') row (mirroring leave() at :75-81), and carry a flash message that the admin panel renders so the transition is visible rather than a bare redirect()->back(). Consider requiring POST + confirmation for a destructive action currently reachable by GET.
proposed_changes.reason: H1's silence is the defect: revokeTracked() + forget('admin_impersonator') + redirect()->back() with no log, no message, and no UI change leaves the admin clicking a button that now 403s, and leaves us unable to reconstruct the incident.

proposed_changes.change: Replace the bare abort_unless at :16 with an explicit, surfaced reason (a redirect back to the panel with a notification, or a rendered error view naming 'admin impersonation session required / expired'), and log the rejection so 403s appear in the audit trail alongside successes. Same for the :20 no-assigned-user 404.
proposed_changes.reason: Ticket AC4 requires that intentional blocks show an explicit reason. Today both aborts precede the activity() call at :26, so rejections are invisible in logs and render as bare HTTP error pages in a freshly opened tab.
proposed_changes.consensus: all 4 candidates (fast-pass, c1 AC4, c2 AC4, c3)

proposed_changes.change: Stop treating the origin-shared localStorage slot as the per-tab credential. Either (a) have authHeaders() take the token from the auth store / an explicitly passed value rather than re-reading localStorage on every call, or (b) key the force-login session per tab (sessionStorage or a tab-scoped key) so each force-login tab keeps its own bearer. Whichever is chosen must keep the driver's normal-login rehydrate-on-reload behaviour (main.js:22) working.
proposed_changes.reason: H2: fetch.js:24 re-reads a slot that auth.js:207 overwrites on every force-login, so each new force-login tab silently repoints all older tabs at a different driver.
proposed_changes.ref: fetch.js:24; auth.js:198-211; auth.js:37; auth.js:189-190; main.js:22; lib/track.js:15
proposed_changes.caution: lib/track.js:15 and stores/auth.js:37 also read the shared slot — change all readers together or analytics/boot silently diverge.

proposed_changes.change: Validate the injected payload before booting: if window.__CLARITY_SCOUT_FORCE_AUTH__ is present but token/user/kit are missing or empty, record a signed-out reason and route to /scout/login instead of calling forceAuthenticate() on a malformed object.
proposed_changes.reason: Lines 17-20 check only for the object's existence. Defensive, not diagnostic — see the note below; keep it low priority.
proposed_changes.downgraded_because: Both candidates rated this 'BUGGY' and treated it as a likely cause of the silent failure. Ground truth says it is nearly unreachable: ClarityScoutForceLoginController:24 assigns from ScoutForceTokens::mintFor(), whose return type is a non-nullable string (:41) built from Sanctum's plainTextToken; :18-20 already abort when the driver is absent; and kit comes from a route-bound model. There is no realistic path to a null token in the payload. Worth adding as cheap defence-in-depth, but it should not be presented as the fix.

proposed_changes.change: Add: (1) consecutive force-logins of 3 DIFFERENT drivers in one admin session -> all 3 tokens remain valid; (2) after exitAdminMode(), assert which tokens are revoked and that the gate is reported explicitly; (3) after a re-impersonation, assert only the intended driver's tokens are revoked; (4) two concurrent mints do not orphan a tracked id.
proposed_changes.reason: Confirmed coverage gap. The 10 existing tests (:58,:87,:107,:123,:143,:161,:171,:182,:198,:216) all exercise a SINGLE driver or the duplicate-GET case; none covers multiple distinct drivers in one session.
proposed_changes.ref: existing tests verified by rg; see tests[] below

out_of_scope: Normal driver login (ClarityScoutAuthController::login) — verified at :64/:66 to delete and mint only 'clarity-scout-token', which never matches 'clarity-scout-force-token'
Scout Bird's Eye admin mode — web-session authed (ClarityScoutAdminMiddleware:34), no force token
The 60-minute force-token TTL (ScoutForceTokens:28) — intentional F1 backstop
Service-worker caching of force-login HTML — carve-out verified at public/clarity-scout-sw.js:83-90
Single-login enforcement (whether force-login should evict the driver) — product decision, AC5/Q6
The hardcoded staff allowlist in ImpersonateController:43-54 — do not widen or replace it as part of this fix
Replacing the session gate with a signed URL or a persisted DB flag — rejected, see H5.rejected_fix_warning

acceptance_criteria.item: Reproduced, including the case where the target user has an active session
acceptance_criteria.reason: Core requirement; must cover idle and actively-logged-in drivers. Coexistence is already proven safe at ClarityScoutAuthController:64 and ClarityScoutForceLoginControllerTest:58, so the interesting half is the reverse direction and the multi-tab case.

acceptance_criteria.item: Root cause identified — session/token handling vs single-login enforcement
acceptance_criteria.reason: Still COMPETING-OPEN. Blocked on Q2/Q4/Q5/Q7; H1 is the ranked leader and H2/H3 are confirmed defects regardless.

acceptance_criteria.item: Admin impersonation works reliably, including consecutive impersonations of different users within one admin session
acceptance_criteria.reason: The reported failure. Requires the driver-scoped tracking fix (H3) AND the per-tab credential fix (H2) — either alone leaves a consecutive-impersonation defect standing.

acceptance_criteria.item: Where impersonation is intentionally blocked, UI shows an explicit reason (not a silent fail)
acceptance_criteria.reason: Silent failure is itself the defect. Must cover the :16 403, the :20 404, and the currently-invisible exitAdminMode() transition.

acceptance_criteria.item: Confirm with product whether impersonating a user should kick that user out of their own Scout session
acceptance_criteria.reason: Product: coexist — force-login must not evict driver's clarity-scout-token. Confirm via test that active driver session survives force-login.

acceptance_criteria.item: PR #410 behaviour preserved — duplicate GET does not revoke the live token, force tokens prune to KEEP_PER_DRIVER=3, service worker does not cache force-login HTML, client surfaces a 401 reason
acceptance_criteria.reason: Must not regress the prior fix; pinned by the 10 existing tests.

acceptance_criteria.item: Force-token session tracking is driver-scoped so one exit cannot revoke another driver's live tab
Each force-login tab holds its own bearer; opening a second force-login tab does not repoint the first tab's requests at a different driver
acceptance_criteria.reason: H2, confirmed defect. Escalate to security-relevant if Q3 shows the drivers spanned orgs.

acceptance_criteria.item: Every force-login outcome is audited — successes AND 403/404 rejections — and exitAdminMode() writes an activity row
acceptance_criteria.reason: Today activity() at ClarityScoutForceLoginController:26 runs only after both aborts, and exitAdminMode() logs nothing. This audit hole is why DEV-2596 cannot be diagnosed retroactively; closing it is also the regression detector for H1.
acceptance_criteria.consensus: reconcile-only (fast-pass asked only that the existing log fire on edge cases)

acceptance_criteria.item: Verify the demo environment was running PR #410
acceptance_criteria.reason: ANSWERED from git — no longer an AC. PR #410 (83fb68d24) merged 2026-09-15 18:01 UTC; deploy ac85618e0 at 2026-09-15 18:18 UTC contains it (git merge-base --is-ancestor). All four 2026-09-16 deploys also contain it. The demo ran post-#410 code.

questions.q: Was the Premier Adjusters demo environment running the PR #410 deploy at the time of the incident?
questions.answer: YES. PR #410 = 83fb68d24, merged 2026-09-15 18:01:32 UTC. Deploy commit ac85618e0 (2026-09-15 18:18:01 UTC) contains it, confirmed with `git merge-base --is-ancestor 83fb68d24 ac85618e0`. All four 2026-09-16 deploys (d777c5711 14:09, 005b23581 16:23, 66163d981 16:45, 397cdd0c3 17:37 UTC) also contain it. The demo ran post-#410 code, ~17h after deploy.
questions.note: All four candidates left this as needs-human. Resolved by reconcile.

questions.q: Did the admin re-impersonate (a fresh Backyard /auth/impersonate) between the working force-login and the 3 failures, or was it all one continuous impersonation?
questions.answer: unknown — not in ticket; no demo witness detail. Proceed without ranking H1 vs idle-session on this fact.
questions.why_blocking: This is the discriminator that promotes or eliminates H3. A re-impersonation hits ImpersonateController:32 -> revokeTracked() -> cross-driver mass revocation. Without it, H3 cannot have fired at all.

questions.q: Were the 3 Scout users in the same org or different orgs?
questions.answer: unknown — not in ticket. Treat same-org as default for repro; keep H2 cross-org severity as residual risk.
questions.why_blocking: Different orgs forces a re-impersonation (feeding Q2/H3) AND escalates H2 from a UX defect to a cross-org data-display defect during a customer demo.

questions.q: Did the admin keep prior force-login tabs open while opening subsequent users, or close each tab first? And did the admin click 'Exit Admin Mode' or 'Leave' at any point?
questions.answer: unknown — not in ticket. Still fix H1 (exit-admin mass-revoke + silent 403) as confirmed defect regardless.
questions.why_blocking: Tabs-open is the precondition for H2. The Exit Admin Mode half is the precondition for H1, the ranked-leading hypothesis, and cannot be recovered from logs because exitAdminMode() writes no activity row.

questions.q: What exactly did 'stopped loading' look like — a 403/404 error page, a blank tab, a spinner that never resolved, or a rendered Scout UI showing the wrong or no data?
questions.answer: unknown — ticket says fails with no error / would no longer load. Cover both silent 403 and silent wrong-boot paths in fix+tests.
questions.why_blocking: Single highest-value unknown. A 403 page points at H1/H4-residual (the gate). A rendered-but-wrong UI points at H2. A tab that rendered then bounced to login points at H3. These have different fixes.

questions.q: Product decision: should admin force-login evict the driver's own live Scout session, or should both coexist?
questions.answer: Coexist — admin force-login must NOT evict the driver's own live Scout session (clarity-scout-token).
questions.why_blocking: Ticket AC5. Current code coexists — grounded at ClarityScoutAuthController:64 (deletes only 'clarity-scout-token') and pinned by ClarityScoutForceLoginControllerTest:58. Cannot be resolved in code.

questions.q: Were any of the 3 target drivers actively logged in on their own devices at the time?
questions.answer: unknown — not in ticket. AC still requires a repro case with an active driver session; implement/test that path.
questions.why_blocking: Ticket AC1 explicitly names this case. Also needed to rule out driver-initiated login as a confound (it is not, per Q10, but the incident timeline should confirm it was not a factor).

questions.q: Does ScoutForceTokens::mintFor()'s Session::push accumulate token ids across consecutive force-logins of different drivers?
questions.answer: YES. ScoutForceTokens.php:49 pushes onto a single flat array with no driver scoping; revokeTracked() (:62,:68) pulls the whole array and bulk-deletes every id. prune() (:75-92) is correctly scoped to $driver->tokens() and KEEP_PER_DRIVER=3 is per-driver, so different drivers never prune each other.

Exactly 3 call sites, all in ImpersonateController: :32 (new impersonation), :83 (leave), :94 (exitAdminMode). Verified with rg across the repo excluding public/build. NOT called on the force-login path — so consecutive force-logins inside one impersonation never trigger revocation. This is what demotes H3 from root cause to contributing defect.

questions.q: Does normal driver login interfere with force tokens?
questions.answer: NO. ClarityScoutAuthController:64 runs $user->tokens()->where('name','clarity-scout-token')->delete() and :66 mints 'clarity-scout-token'. Exact-match on name, so 'clarity-scout-force-token' is untouched. Confirmed by direct read. Logout (:97) deletes only currentAccessToken(), so a driver signing out does not touch the admin's force token either.
questions.note: All 4 candidates claimed this and all 4 were right. A Grep-tool false negative initially appeared to contradict them — see reconcile_notes.tooling_caveat.

questions.q: Can a new tab fail to receive the admin's session cookie (C2)?
questions.answer: NO. config/session.php: same_site='lax' (:202), path='/' (:146), partitioned=false (:215). shouldOpenInNewTab produces a same-origin top-level GET navigation, precisely the case SameSite=Lax allows, and browser tabs share one cookie jar — the session cookie is not tab-scoped. C2 is refuted.

questions.q: Can admin_impersonator be lost mid-flow to session()->invalidate() (C1)?
questions.answer: NO as stated. ImpersonateController::impersonate() invalidates at :35 and re-puts admin_impersonator at :57 within the same request, before the redirect at :69 — atomic from any other request's point of view. Two residual variants stay open and are tracked on H4: the 120-minute idle session expiry (config/session.php:35) and the concurrent-mint session-write clobber.

questions.q: Does the PR #410 service-worker change prevent the original bug recurring?
questions.answer: YES. public/clarity-scout-sw.js:83-90 excludes /scout/force-login (and /scout/org-map) from the navigation shell cache, so HTML embedding a live bearer is never written to disk and cannot be replayed onto a revoked token. CLEAR_API_CACHE (:62-66) separately purges the API cache.

questions.q: Is there any payload validation in the Scout PWA for the injected forceAuth object?
questions.answer: NO — main.js:17-20 checks only that window.__CLARITY_SCOUT_FORCE_AUTH__ exists. But the gap is near-unreachable: mintFor() returns a non-nullable string (ScoutForceTokens:41), the driver is abort-guarded (ClarityScoutForceLoginController:18-20), and the kit is route-bound. Keep as defence-in-depth, not as the fix. Contradicts fast-pass and candidate-3, which both graded this 'BUGGY' and treated it as a likely silent-failure cause.

questions.q: Is Echo/broadcast channel auth affected by the shared-localStorage token swap (H2)?
questions.answer: NO, and that makes H2 worse rather than better. connectEcho() bakes the token into the Echo config's Authorization header at construction time (lib/echo.js:38-43) and never re-reads localStorage, so each tab's realtime channel stays bound to the driver it was opened for, while its REST calls follow the shared localStorage slot. Result is a split-brain tab: realtime on driver A, REST on driver C. channels.php:22 would reject a mismatched token ((int)$user->id !== $userId), so if Echo DID re-read the slot the subscription would 403 on /api/broadcasting/auth — a path that bypasses handleUnauthorized() entirely (it is wired only into fetch.js) and would surface no reason at all.

questions.q: Is the force-login route protected by anything beyond 'auth'?
questions.answer: NO. routes/web.php:105 — Route::get('scout/force-login/{kit}', ...)->middleware('auth'), inside a config('app.experimental.clarity_scout') block. No signed-URL, throttle, or CSRF middleware. The only staff gate is the in-controller session check at ClarityScoutForceLoginController:16. This is why H5's proposal to remove that check is unsafe.
questions.note: Candidate-2 raised this as an open question; resolved.

notes: TIMELINE SETTLED: PR #410 (83fb68d24) merged 2026-09-15 18:01 UTC, deployed 18:18 UTC the same day (ac85618e0). The 2026-09-16 demo ran post-#410 code. The 'suspicious timing' framing all four candidates built on ('ticket filed the day after the merge — was it even deployed?') is resolved: it was deployed, so this is a NEW failure mode, not an undeployed fix.

H1 (reconcile-only, ranked leader): GET /auth/impersonate/exit-admin is a one-click, unconfirmed, unlogged, GET-reachable action that revokes every tracked force token AND strips the force-login gate, then redirect()->back() so nothing visibly changes and the stale Livewire table keeps rendering the button. Best single explanation for 'worked, then stopped for 3 consecutive users, no error'.

H2 (reconcile-only): the Scout PWA's bearer lives in origin-shared localStorage. fetch.js:24 re-reads it per request; auth.js:207 overwrites it per force-login. Multi-tab force-login therefore cross-contaminates driver identity, silently, with a 200 response — because ClarityScoutMiddleware:25 treats the force ability as a hard bypass of the kit/permission/feature checks and happily serves whichever driver owns the token.

H3 demoted: revokeTracked() is called ONLY from ImpersonateController:32/:83/:94 (rg-verified). Consecutive force-logins within one impersonation never call it. Candidate-3 rated its cross-driver-revocation root cause at 85 confidence while attributing a symptom that its own mechanism could not produce — the clearest instance in this merge of confident-over-grounded.
Echo is per-tab (token baked in at lib/echo.js:40) while REST is origin-shared (fetch.js:24). Any fix must not leave those two disagreeing.

AUDIT HOLE: activity() in ClarityScoutForceLoginController sits at :26, after the :16 403 and the :20 404. Only successes are logged. exitAdminMode() logs nothing at all, unlike leave() (:75-81). Closing both is cheap, is required by AC4's spirit, and is the regression detector for H1.

GATE-BYPASS BREADTH: the 'clarity-scout-force' ability short-circuits before the permission, kit_id, and CLARITY_SCOUT feature checks in BOTH ClarityScoutMiddleware:25-27 and routes/channels.php:30-32. Any change to how the force token is minted, scoped, or revoked must consider both. channels.php:22 additionally pins the channel to the token's own user id.

CONCURRENCY: Session::push at ScoutForceTokens:49 has no request-level locking. Two near-simultaneous force-login GETs (the very prefetch/double-click case PR #410 was written for) can have the later session write clobber the earlier, orphaning a token id so it is never revoked on exit — a gate-bypassing credential surviving to its 60-min TTL. grounding.code_flow: Admin arrives from Backyard via a Black-Adam-signed GET /auth/impersonate. ImpersonateController revokes any tracked force tokens, invalidates and regenerates the session, logs in as the target user, puts 'impersonator' always and 'admin_impersonator' only for the 10 allowlisted staff ids — all in one request. In the Filament panel, ScoutUsersResource renders a 'Login to Scout' action whose visibility depends on admin_impersonator; clicking opens /scout/force-login/{kit} in a NEW TAB. That route ('auth' middleware only) checks admin_impersonator or 403s, resolves the kit's assigned driver or 404s, mints a 60-minute Sanctum token with the clarity-scout-force ability, pushes its id onto a flat session array, prunes the driver to 3 tokens, logs an activity row, and renders the PWA with the token inlined. main.js calls auth.forceAuthenticate(), which purges the shared SW API cache, writes the bearer into ORIGIN-SHARED localStorage, and opens an Echo connection with the token baked in. From then on every REST call re-reads that shared slot (fetch.js:24) while Echo stays pinned to the token it was built with. REVOCATION happens only from ImpersonateController — :32 on a new impersonation, :83 on leave, :94 on exitAdminMode — and each one deletes EVERY id in the flat array, across all drivers. FAILURE SURFACE: (H1) one GET to /auth/impersonate/exit-admin strips admin_impersonator and mass-revokes, then returns the admin to an unchanged-looking page whose stale table still offers a button that now 403s in a fresh tab. (H2) each additional force-login tab overwrites the shared bearer, so older tabs silently authenticate as the newest driver and — because the force ability bypasses the kit/permission/feature checks — receive 200s full of the wrong driver's data. (H3) after a re-impersonation or exit, every open tab's token dies at once; REST 401s do route through handleUnauthorized and would surface a reason, but Echo-auth failures never do.

confidence_rationale: Higher than any single candidate on the DEFECT INVENTORY and lower than candidate-3's 85 on ROOT CAUSE, deliberately. Grounded gains: the deploy question is settled from git; two of three competing hypotheses are refuted from code; the third is demoted with a call-site proof; two previously unseen defects (H1 exit-admin silence, H2 cross-tab token collision) are confirmed with file:line; the test gap and audit hole are verified. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated and honest: nobody knows what 'stopped loading' actually was on the wire (Q5), whether the admin re-impersonated or exited admin mode (Q2/Q4), and exitAdminMode() logs nothing so the incident cannot be reconstructed from data. The three confirmed defects can be fixed and tested without resolving that, but AC2 cannot be closed. Candidate-3's 85 was over-confident — it named a root cause whose own mechanism could not have fired in the reported scenario.

escalate.reason: Three independent grounds. (1) Blast radius: this is auth/session code whose token hard-bypasses the kit, permission, and feature-flag gates in two places (ClarityScoutMiddleware:25, channels.php:30) — a mistake either locks staff out or leaves a gate-bypassing credential alive, and one proposed candidate fix (replacing the session check with a signed URL) would have removed the only staff gate on the route. (2) Unresolved attribution: root cause is competing-open and the discriminating facts live with the demo operator, not in the code; a 5-minute interview (Q2/Q4/Q5) is worth more than further static analysis. (3) H2 may be a cross-org data-display defect, not just a UX bug — if the 3 demo drivers spanned orgs (Q3), a tab labelled one org's driver was showing another org's driver data in front of a customer, which needs a security-aware call on severity and disclosure. Also: AC5 needs a product decision, and pairing with the PR #410 author (Dalton, 83fb68d24) is advisable since the fix reshapes the session-tracking mechanism that PR introduced.

disagreed_and_how_settled.positions: C-fast/C3 = Session::push cross-driver revocation (c3 at 85 confidence); C1 = admin_impersonator lost to session invalidate -> silent 403; C2 = new-tab session/cookie propagation -> intermittent 403.
disagreed_and_how_settled.settled: All three settled AGAINST from ground truth, and the field re-ranked. C2 refuted by config/session.php (same_site=lax, path=/, same-origin top-level GET; tabs share the cookie jar) and by its own lack of any file:line — grounded beats confident. C1 refuted because ImpersonateController invalidates (:35) and re-puts admin_impersonator (:57) in one atomic request. C3 demoted, not refuted: the defect is real at :49/:62/:68, but rg proves revokeTracked() is never called from the force-login path, so it cannot fire on consecutive force-logins inside one impersonation. Root cause status therefore stays COMPETING-OPEN, now with a reconcile-found leader (H1, exit-admin) and a reconcile-found confirmed defect (H2, cross-tab localStorage) that outrank all three original hypotheses.

disagreed_and_how_settled.point: Should ImpersonateController's revokeTracked() move to after session()->invalidate()?
disagreed_and_how_settled.positions: fast-pass and c3 both proposed reordering, worrying the array 'might persist in memory'.
disagreed_and_how_settled.settled: REJECTED. The current order is correct — revokeTracked() must read the array before invalidate() destroys it. Reordering would make revocation a silent no-op and leak every force token. The candidates' stated reason ('might persist in memory') is not a real mechanism in Laravel's request-scoped session. A genuine concern in the same area is kept instead: unlocked concurrent session writes can orphan a tracked id (H4 variant).
